body: Yes Bank peaked near Rs 393-404 in Aug 2018 and hit ~Rs 5.6 on 6 Mar 2020 (-98%) after RBI superseded the board and imposed a moratorium (withdrawals capped at Rs 50,000) on 5 Mar 2020. An SBI-led consortium recapitalised it at Rs 10/share; Rs 8,415 cr of AT1 bonds were written off; ~75% of existing shares were locked in for 3 years. Visible flags well before: (1) RBI-assessed NPA divergence: ~Rs 4,177 cr in FY16 and ~Rs 6,355 cr in FY17 (reported NPAs were a fraction of RBI's); (2) loan book growing 30-35%/yr with corporate concentration in stressed groups (ADAG, Essel, DHFL, IL&FS, Cox & Kings, Jet, CG Power); (3) low CASA and dependence on bulk/high-cost deposits; (4) Sep 2018 RBI refused to extend founder Rana Kapoor's term -- a regulator vote of no confidence; (5) promoter shares pledged and sold by lenders; (6) independent director exit in Jan 2019; GNPA jumped from 1.3% (FY18) to 3.2% (FY19) to 7.4% (Sep 2019). Who spotted it: RBI inspections (divergence disclosures were public from 2017), some short-side analysts. Lesson: for banks, divergence disclosures, concentration to stressed groups and regulator actions on management are disqualifiers; 'cheap' P/B after the first fall is a value trap.

data.early_signals: RBI NPA divergence FY16/FY17; RBI cut CEO tenure Sep 2018; group-exposure concentration; pledged promoter shares
data.lesson: Divergence = understated NPAs; regulator acting on CEO is a sell signal

title: Yes Bank: hidden NPAs and RBI moratorium (2018-2020)

body: Split-adjusted (3:1, Nov 2023): ~$1-1.5 in early 2020 [unverified] -> ~$99 (Mar-May 2024; YTD high $98.72 in May): ~60-70x. Driver: 'better-for-you' fitness energy drink sold to young women/gym users, then the Aug 2022 PepsiCo long-term US distribution deal (Pepsi invested ~$550m for ~8.5% [unverified]) that put Celsius in Pepsi's DSD network nationwide; revenue roughly tripled 2022-23 [unverified]. Mostly revenue/EPS growth, but P/E also peaked near 100x [unverified]. Reversal: Pepsi had over-ordered and then destocked — Q3 2024 revenue -31% to $266m, net income -92% — while retail scanner sales still grew ~7%; Alani Nu, Ghost and others took share; stock -73% (May-Sept 2024 to ~$32), -52% in 2024, low ~$21 early 2025 [unverified]. Feb 2025: bought Alani Nu for $1.8bn (cash + $500m stock), stock +~20-30%; closed Apr 1 2025. EARLY SIGNAL (up): distribution step-change into a national DSD system, measured in scanner data before reported revenue. EARLY SIGNAL (down): reported revenue running far ahead of scanner sell-through in 2023-24 — distributor inventory build. Who caught it: retail/momentum; no documented famous name. LESSON: a distribution deal gives a one-time step change; when sell-in (reported sales) outruns sell-through (scanner data), the destocking reversal is predictable — a direct echo of Monster's playbook but at a much higher price.

data.early_signals: up: Pepsi DSD deal 2022; down: sell-in > scanner sell-through
data.lesson: distribution step change is one-time; monitor scanner vs reported sales
